page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-16 is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B45 processor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is configured with 30.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 1.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache architecture includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results show top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 10% of tested instances. Single-threaded operations, such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, also register in the top 10%. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached and uncached reads/writes align with average tier performance, as do database operations and static web serving throughput. For machine learning workloads, the instance demonstrates top-tier text generation speeds on small (135M) LLM models, though performance scales down to average levels on medium (7B) models.

The c4d-highcpu-16 presents a clear tradeoff: it delivers exceptional single-threaded compute capabilities but is constrained by a low memory-to-vCPU ratio and the complete absence of local NVMe storage. This makes it highly cost-efficient for compute-heavy workloads that do not require large memory footprints or high-speed local disk I/O. It is well-suited for single-threaded processing tasks, text processing, lightweight LLM inference, and compute-bound batch processing. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale multi-threaded compilation tasks.
